title: 10-minute agent-focused presentation built on KEY-1879
summary: Cut the existing 17-slide 'Treating AI Like Untrusted Code' deck (claude-code-shared/ai_architecture_presentation.html) into a new, separate 9-slide, exactly 10:00 deck for an internal engineering audience. The agents are the cast. One real Quaestor-Web feature, KEY-1879 (the portco TopBar and Tabs cutover, merged 2026-07-31 as PR #18097), is followed through the pipeline agents: grill-me, to-seed and the 4 critics, to-tasks, build-runner with Haiku verifiers, pr-code-review, pr-revise, and the learning loop. Each middle slide is one agent at work with one real artifact. Engagement comes from the story plus a show-of-hands opener. The focus stays on what the agents do, not on the author's misses. Real names, files and screenshots are allowed on screen.
problem_statement: The existing deck has 17 slides, no timing, and spreads agent content across three separate diagrams (slides 10-12) with no single story connecting them. It cannot be delivered in 10 minutes, and it does not make the agents the focus.
solution: A new HTML deck with 9 slides, no speaker notes, reusing the current deck's CSS, keyboard/swipe/progress-bar navigation and inline-SVG style. The thesis is 'Treat agents like untrusted code: one job each, a typed contract, a different agent checks the work, and the system learns.' A single real feature, KEY-1879, is the through-line. Each pipeline agent appears when it does its job on that feature.
decisions: Target length is exactly 10:00 across 9 slides. The 17-slide deck is kept unchanged as the long version.

Build the 10-minute deck as a NEW file, proposed name claude-code-shared/agents_10min_presentation.html. Reuse the existing deck's CSS theme, nav script and SVG diagram style. Do not cut the existing file in place.
No speaker notes and no presenter clock. The author will rehearse to time.
Audience is internal engineers. Show real artifacts: real screenshot, real file names, real claims, real JSON and log snippets from KEY-1879. No sanitizing or renaming.
Thesis: 'Treat agents like untrusted code: one job each, a typed contract, a different agent checks the work, and the system learns.' The agents are the proof of the thesis, not a catalog tour.
Engagement device: follow ONE real feature through the agents as a story. Each agent appears when needed, so there is no catalog. A live demo and a failure gallery were not chosen.
Hero feature is KEY-1879, the portco TopBar and Tabs cutover (PR #18097, July 2026). The /ci-fix skill (dotfiles) and the date-field work (KEY-2318, PR #19659) were considered and not chosen.
Framing: agents are the heroes, each doing its own job. Catches are shown as proof the design works. Do not frame them as the author's misses, failures or reliance on the system.
Slide 1, Hook (0:30): 'Junior dev with root access' hook plus a show of hands: 'Who's had an AI tell you it ran the tests when it didn't?'

Slide 2, Meet the team (1:00): slim pipeline diagram with each agent and its model tier labeled, plus the real KEY-1879 TopBar screenshot. An optional audience guess 'how many agents touched this PR?' may be kept or dropped in rehearsal. The user's pick of the show of hands over the guess was tentative ('maybe the latter? idk'), so the show of hands is the default.

Slide 3, grill-me, to-seed and the 4 critics (1:30): the 07-15 grill found a hidden 9th route (investment-details-beta riding on Company.tsx). The seed had 21 decisions, then the critics screened it. Artifact: a seed JSON snippet.
Slide 4, to-tasks and build-runner (1:30): typed task contracts, then a red-green-refactor build, with Haiku verifiers running lint and tests. Artifact: the build log line showing 2211 passed.

Slide 5, pr-code-review (1:00): a separate reviewer agent reviews the author's work and flags the isHydrated state leak across company switches (learning row 942c2e1d, 2026-07-24). Artifact: the finding itself. This is agent-checks-agent proof.

Slide 6, pr-revise (1:30): the 07-30 round turned 10 review threads (2 Cursor Bugbot, 8 human) into a seed, then 18 tasks (8 code, 10 reply drafts), with no hand triage. Artifact: the thread-to-task mapping.

Slide 7, the learning loop (1:30): Cursor Bugbot flagged the dropped key= remount (state leaking across company switches, 07-27). pr-revise recorded it as learning 18bc42e9 on 07-28 (cause_label candidate, improves grill-me). Commit 1f7325714d fixed the code, and the learning became a rule at grill-me/SKILL.md:46 (deletion audit for key= remounts). The slide may show attribution-tracer and the artifact-grounding-judge as the general loop mechanism, but must not claim either one ran on or verified this specific learning: the trail records attribution-tracer firing only once, for the 07-31 seed's confirmed_escape. Reveal: 'I planned this talk with that same grill skill. It asked me about deleted components because of this bug.' Do not say 'root cause proven'.

Slide 8, Steal these (1:00): three takeaways. (1) One agent, one job, with a typed contract (seed.json, task.json, runner-result.json). (2) The author never checks its own work. A different agent verifies, and verification runs on a cheap tier. (3) Every escape becomes a rule, via the learning loop to a file:line in a skill.
Slide 9, Close (0:30): 'Disagree? Good.' Time budget in order: 0:30, 1:00, 1:30, 1:30, 1:00, 1:30, 1:30, 1:00, 0:30, which sums to 10:00.

Cut from the long deck: slides 2-7 (folded into the story), slide 13 (principles table), slide 14 (why local), and the diagrams on slides 9-12 as standalone slides. Agent content appears inside the story beats.
The unsourced percentage claims on old slide 16 ('40% token cut', '80% to Haiku', '13 blocking gates') are cut. They have no source in this story and invite measurement questions.

The slide 2 screenshot is a real screenshot the user took of a portco page in the app (TopBar with tabs, seeded fake company data). It is embedded in the HTML as a base64 data URI so the deck stays a single file. A copy was saved at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-eric--dotfiles/40be86b9-8726-4976-85a5-19ebbceaaa0c/scratchpad/key-1879-topbar.png (original 2008x218). The original was in a macOS temp folder.
